action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies support the diagnosis and show the demyelinating or axonal pattern; a normal study in the first week does not exclude GBS [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis and excludes the infectious and malignant causes of polyradiculopathy that raise the cell count [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; abnormal liver tests or low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course; no metabolic or toxic alternative
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests exclude metabolic mimics (potassium, glucose, CK) and give the baseline before IVIg; liver tests and albumin carry prognostic weight [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: She is still progressing with facial and bulbar involvement; serial FVC, MIP and MEP decide when ICU-level monitoring is needed [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus tachycardia while awake, a self-limited sinus bradycardia to 52 bpm during sleep and blood pressure 122/76 to 156/94 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias, pauses and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sinus tachycardia 102 bpm with normal intervals (QTc 448 ms) and no conduction or ST-T abnormality: a baseline while autonomic involvement can still develop
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic dysrhythmia and conduction abnormality and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No current medications, so no interaction with IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.label: Optional interaction check before IVIg or plasma exchange (no current medications)
action_criteria.rationale: She takes no medicines, so the check cannot change management.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on IVIg versus plasma exchange in GBS
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
required_recommendations: Admit to a monitored bed with serial FVC, MIP and MEP every 4-6 hours and bedside swallow and cough assessment (she has dysarthria); move to ICU-level monitoring if FVC falls below 60% predicted or 20 mL/kg (about 1.3 L at 67 kg), MIP becomes weaker than -40 cmH2O, MEP falls below 40 cmH2O, FVC falls by more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough or pooled secretions develops [EAN_PNS_2023, Lawn_2001].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 27 g/day at 67 kg) now, within 2 weeks of onset, because she cannot walk unaided (GBS disability score 3); plasma exchange (200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions) is an equivalent alternative [EAN_PNS_2023].
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses.
Pharmacological DVT prophylaxis (subcutaneous low-molecular-weight heparin) while she cannot walk unaided [Leonhard_2019].

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, long-tract signs, a brainstem syndrome). A lower motor neuron facial palsy with an areflexic polyradiculoneuropathy does not call for it.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome (acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy) after a diarrheal illness

differential.key_features: Cannot be excluded at presentation; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.
Facial palsy with radicular symptoms occurs in neuroborreliosis, but the CSF has 4 cells/mm3 (neuroborreliosis gives a lymphocytic pleocytosis), and no tick bite or erythema migrans is reported.
Areflexia, no sensory level, no sphincter dysfunction and facial involvement are not explained by a cord lesion.
Symmetric rather than multifocal deficits, demyelinating NCS, no systemic vasculitic features.

key_clinical_evidence: Bilateral limb weakness with areflexia, CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 58 mg/dL, 4 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating NCS: Brighton level 1 once the course plateaus within 4 weeks [Brighton_2011].

The diarrheal illness 2 weeks before onset is a history finding and counts in the mEGOS prognostic score; serology is not needed for the diagnosis, and a positive IgM does not prove the trigger [Walgaard_2011].
Anti-ganglioside antibodies are not needed to diagnose typical GBS; anti-GQ1b is tested when Miller Fisher syndrome or an overlap is suspected [EAN_PNS_2023].
She cannot walk unaided (GBS disability score 3) at day 8, so IVIg or plasma exchange is indicated now [EAN_PNS_2023].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Facial involvement in GBS can be unilateral or asymmetric. The palsy is lower motor neuron with no long-tract signs, and the bilateral limb weakness, areflexia, CSF albuminocytological dissociation with 4 cells/mm3 and demyelinating NCS place it within the polyradiculoneuropathy.
red_herrings.data_point: Unilateral left lower motor neuron facial palsy
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests Bell's palsy, a brainstem lesion or Lyme disease, and marked asymmetry counts against GBS

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

findings.finding: DML 6.4 ms (prolonged); CV 40 m/s (reduced); CMAP 4.1 mV
DML 8.2 ms (prolonged); CV 32 m/s (reduced); CMAP 2.8 mV
Absent bilateral peroneal; prolonged median (58 ms)
Tibialis anterior, vastus lateralis and first dorsal interosseous bilaterally: reduced recruitment of normal-morphology motor units; no fibrillation potentials or positive sharp waves

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Prolonged distal motor latencies and reduced conduction velocities in bilateral median and peroneal motor nerves. 2. Absent sural sensory nerve action potentials bilaterally; reduced median sensory amplitudes. 3. Absent F-waves bilaterally (peroneal); prolonged F-wave latency (58 ms) in bilateral median nerves. 4. Absent H-reflex bilaterally. 5. Reduced recruitment without denervation on needle EMG. Pattern consistent with a demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions (NCS/EMG, CSF, baseline labs, respiratory function, telemetry), 1 red herring (unilateral facial palsy) that must be placed within the polyradiculoneuropathy.
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Eight-day progressive bilateral leg weakness with unilateral facial weakness and areflexia, preceded by diarrheal illness.
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. K. is a 45-year-old woman with an 8-day history of progressive bilateral leg weakness following a diarrheal illness 2 weeks prior. She can still walk with support but weakness has progressed daily. She has noticed drooping of the left side of her face and mildly slurred speech. Distal paresthesias are present.

neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Left lower motor neuron facial weakness involving forehead and lower face; right face normal. Mild dysarthria. Eye movements full, no ptosis. Palate elevates symmetrically.
neurological_exam.gait: Can walk 15 feet with single-hand support.
neurological_exam.motor: Bilateral lower extremity weakness: hip flexion 3+/5, knee extension 4/5, ankle dorsiflexion 4/5. Upper extremity: 4/5 bilateral.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Absent bilateral Achilles. Absent bilateral patellar. Trace bilateral biceps and brachioradialis.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral distal paresthesias. Reduced vibration at ankles.
